answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because karst only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, beacon is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
